a.text: Funny how the Green Harbor Party suddenly loves “affordable energy” after backing every turbine plan from the Luma lobby. Before anyone buys their new speech, ask this: can we really trust their numbers when their campaign team met with Voltaro consultants last month? The River Coal Alliance at least says plainly it wants cheaper bills and local jobs. Green Harbor keeps wrapping higher costs in pretty words and hoping nobody checks the details. Share if you are tired of being treated like a meter, not a citizen.

a.text: Election week in Briarford and the Civic Dawn Party wants applause for its “clean campaign.” Please. Their mailers are a slick little smear machine, and now they expect voters to forget who paid for them. Before you mark a ballot, ask yourself: can anyone trust Civic Dawn’s observers after their coordinator mixed up precinct lists twice? The Northgate Reform Bloc may be loud, but at least it is not pretending confusion is transparency. Don’t reward theater and then act shocked when city hall feels staged.

a.text: The Maple Gate Movement keeps pretending its migration plan is kindness, but people in East Veyra can see the chaotic border gamble for what it is. We are past polite slogans now: either we pause new arrivals or lose control of our towns. The Open Path League is at least honest that services need limits before more promises are made. Maple Gate wants applause from commentators while local schools and clinics carry the pressure. If that sounds responsible to you, I have a bridge in Nollhaven to sell.

a.text: Every time peace talks in Norvask get close, the Iron Shield Front finds a new excuse to cheer more shelling. Their leaders sold Briarmere a blood-soaked fantasy and now act surprised that families are burying sons. Let’s stop pretending this is complicated: the war continues because Iron Shield refuses peace. The Lantern Peace Council is at least calling for talks before another winter wrecks the border villages. If Iron Shield had to visit every grieving kitchen, maybe the speeches would get shorter.

a.text: The Brookmere Electoral Office said voting will begin at 7 a.m. on Sunday in the municipal election. The Silver List is campaigning on rent controls and expanded bus routes, while the Amber Bloc is emphasizing lower business fees and road repairs. Both sides held events in East Quay on Thursday, and observers from the Civic Register will monitor selected polling stations. Final results are expected late Monday after mailed ballots are counted.

a.text: In Port Avelin, the Harbor Party proposed opening a new reception center for migrant families, while the Meadow Coalition called for a smaller registration office and more funding for language classes. The city council scheduled a public hearing for next Tuesday at the Old Market Hall. Officials said current arrivals are being housed in temporary rooms near the station, and local charities have asked residents to donate winter clothing before the end of the month.

a.text: The Rivermark Health Board met Friday to review two proposals for expanding evening clinic hours. The Lantern Group supports adding shifts at district clinics first, while the Cedar Forum wants to begin with a mobile nursing team for outer villages. Board chair Mira Solven said staff costs and patient travel times will be compared before a vote in March. The regional hospital will continue its current weekend service during the review period.
